modern: Do you have reason? I have.—Why then do you not use it? For if this does its own work, what else do you want?
original: Hast thou reason? I have.—Why then dost not thou use it? For if this does its own work, what else dost thou wish?

explained.summary: A quick exchange with himself. Do you have reason? Yes. Then why not use it? If your reason is doing its job, Marcus says, you have everything you need. The problem is rarely a lack of good sense, only a failure to apply it.
